How to read AEC

Start by naming the exact product surface, version, channel, and delivery you mean. Then check what the publisher sources say, where each statement applies, and what those sources leave unknown.

Compare records Browse records

1. Name the product surface before comparing it

The same product family can contain a local CLI, an IDE extension, and a hosted service. A claim for one does not automatically apply to the others.

OpenAI Codex CLI0.150.1 · Local
Codex cloud agentRolling service · Hosted
Codex IDE extensionRolling service · Hybrid
Publisher
Named publisher
Surface
CLI, IDE extension, cloud worker, or another named surface
Version
Exact version or rolling-service scope
Channel
Recorded when a source identifies one
Delivery
Local, hybrid, or hosted

2. Check what publisher sources say

AEC records statements from named publisher-controlled sources. Every displayed claim links back to its source and remains attached to the exact record that source supports.

  1. Publisher documentationA specific statement in a publisher-controlled source.
  2. Publisher sourceThe named page, release, or document where the statement appears.
  3. Where it appliesThe version, settings, platform, model, or deployment conditions attached to the statement.

3. Read where each claim applies

A statement may apply only to one version, operating system, model, configuration, or deployment mode. AEC keeps those conditions beside the claim so similar product names do not erase meaningful differences.

4. Treat unknown as a source gap, not capability absence

If a fact is missing, unresolved, or outside the admitted publisher sources, AEC leaves it unknown. Unknown means “these sources do not establish this,” not “the product lacks this capability.”

Publisher-documented topicExact record AExact record B
StatementShown with its publisher sourceNo publisher claim documented in this category
MeaningVersion and conditions remain visibleNo capability conclusion is inferred

5. Follow earlier and later records for the same surface

Exact records are not overwritten when a surface changes. Predecessor and successor links preserve which version was reviewed, what replaced it, and which record is current within the dated catalog view.

6. Understand what AEC does not establish

AEC organizes publisher documentation. It does not establish:

  • Observed behaviorNo product was installed or run for these source-only records.
  • QualityDocumentation coverage is not a quality measure.
  • SafetyPublisher claims and visible unknowns are not a safety finding.
  • SuitabilityThe catalog does not decide whether an agent fits your task or environment.
  • Independent testsEvery current record includes zero admitted independent tests.
  • A winnerAEC does not score, rank, recommend, or certify products.

7. Read snapshot and review dates

The dated catalog view says which records belong to this snapshot. The source-review seal says when the admitted publisher material was last closed for review. Later releases may exist; they do not silently change a reviewed record.

  1. Dated catalog viewA stable point of reference for the included records.
  2. Source review sealedThe UTC time when the admitted source set closed for this view.
  3. Later release reviewed separatelyA record changes only after another human source review.

Check a source or correct a public factual error

Each record page links its displayed publisher claims to named sources. Public-safe factual corrections may be proposed for human review; intake remains closed and this repository cannot receive sensitive reports.
